limitations: All-time guard replay reconstructs numerical target projection only; no controller or physical trajectory is replayed.
The guard can directly change every input row via fullK joint-velocity columns, including shaft row; it does not impose actual speed/acceleration bounds.

Nominal material joint references integrate guarded rates, but native feedback explicitly zeroes shell material-angle errors and replaces shaft angle error with rolling position/pitch relation; not a direct shaft material-angle servo.
Only saved reference residuals on modified rows are used. Residuals describe reference geometry, not actual no-slip or torque feasibility.
Lean and command histories can show entering-state chronology, not identify a unique full-trajectory physical cause.
